dietEvidence.body: The beak and dental battery indicate herbivory. No gut contents are known; the plants eaten and the feeding style are inferred from jaw anatomy.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A large iguanodontian with a deep skull, a thumb spike and a robust body. The Bernissart skeletons transformed early ideas about dinosaur posture.
summary: A large iguanodontian with a deep skull, a thumb spike and a robust body. The Bernissart skeletons transformed early ideas about dinosaur posture.

discovery.body: Named by Boulenger, 1881. The record is known from Sainte-Barbe Clays, Bernissart. Many articulated skeletons from Bernissart, plus material from other European localities.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The Sainte-Barbe Clays at Bernissart produced many articulated skeletons. The bonebed is direct evidence of a mass accumulation; the cause of the accumulation is a separate taphonomic question.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Sainte-Barbe Clays, Bernissart records the species in the Early Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈126–122 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The skull is deep, the dental battery is well developed, and the hand bears a large conical thumb spike. Skin impressions show a scaly covering.

behaviour.body: Many skeletons accumulated at Bernissart, which is consistent with gregarious behaviour but does not prove it. The thumb spike is preserved; its use in defence, feeding or display is inferred.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from many articulated skeletons from Bernissart, plus material from other european localities. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The Bernissart skeletons established much of the anatomy of Iguanodon bernissartensis, including the thumb spike and scaly integument. The bonebed is direct evidence of accumulation; herding is an inference. No gut contents are known.

primer.lead: Iguanodon bernissartensis was a large plant-eating ornithopod from the [Early Cretaceous](/deep-time?period=cretaceous) of Belgium. The amazing Bernissart skeletons transformed early ideas about dinosaur posture and anatomy.
paragraphs: It had a deep skull, a dental battery for processing plants, and a large conical thumb spike. Skin impressions show a scaly covering. Many articulated skeletons were found together at Bernissart, which is consistent with gregarious behaviour, though herding is an inference.
The animal could walk on four legs but also adopt a bipedal stance. The thumb spike’s function — defence, feeding or display — is unresolved, and no gut contents are known.
primer.takeaway: A large, thumb-spiked plant-eater known from a spectacular bonebed.
